import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from lifelines import KaplanMeierFitter
from lifelines.statistics import logrank_test

# 1. Load data
clinical = pd.read_csv('cleaned_clinical_data.csv')
mutations = pd.read_csv('cleaned_mutations.csv')

# 2. Flag patients with ≥1 HIGH-impact mutation
high_imp_patients = set(
    mutations.loc[mutations['IMPACT'] == 'HIGH', 'bcr_patient_barcode']
)

# 3. Create flag
clinical['HighImpact'] = clinical['bcr_patient_barcode'].isin(high_imp_patients)

# 4. Prepare survival data
# Keep patients with known vital status and follow-up times
df = clinical[['bcr_patient_barcode', 'HighImpact', 'vital_status',
               'days_to_death', 'days_to_last_followup']].copy()
# Define time and event
mask_dead = df['vital_status'] == 'Dead'
df['time'] = df['days_to_death'].where(mask_dead, df['days_to_last_followup'])
df['event'] = mask_dead.astype(int)
# Drop missing times or statuses
df = df[df['time'].notna() & df['vital_status'].isin(['Alive', 'Dead'])]

# 5. Kaplan-Meier analysis
groups = df['HighImpact']
time = df['time']
event = df['event']
kmf_hi = KaplanMeierFitter()
kmf_lo = KaplanMeierFitter()

T_hi = time[groups]
E_hi = event[groups]
T_lo = time[~groups]
E_lo = event[~groups]

kmf_hi.fit(T_hi, E_hi, label='HighImpact')
kmf_lo.fit(T_lo, E_lo, label='NoHighImpact')

# 6. Log-rank test
results = logrank_test(T_hi, T_lo, E_hi, E_lo)

# 7. Plot survival curves
plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
ax = plt.subplot(111)
kmf_hi.plot_survival_function(ax=ax)
kmf_lo.plot_survival_function(ax=ax)
plt.title('Overall Survival by High-Impact Mutation Status')
plt.xlabel('Days')
plt.ylabel('Survival Probability')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# 8. Print results
median_hi = kmf_hi.median_survival_time_
median_lo = kmf_lo.median_survival_time_
print(f"Log-rank test: chi-square = {results.test_statistic:.2f}, p-value = {results.p_value:.4f}\n")
print("Median survival times (days):")
print(f"  HighImpact   : {median_hi:.1f}")
print(f"  NoHighImpact : {median_lo:.1f}")
print(f"\nSample sizes: HighImpact = {len(T_hi)}, NoHighImpact = {len(T_lo)}")

review:
Hypothesis: Patients with ≥1 HIGH‐impact somatic mutation have worse overall survival than patients without HIGH‐impact mutations.

Implementation: Clinical and mutation data were loaded. Patients were flagged if they carried any mutation with IMPACT='HIGH'. A time‐to‐event variable was defined using days_to_death for deceased and days_to_last_followup for censored (alive) patients. Kaplan–Meier curves were fit for HighImpact vs NoHighImpact groups, and a log‐rank test was performed. Median survival times and sample sizes were reported, and a survival plot with confidence intervals was generated.

Results: 1,097 patients were analyzed (HighImpact=1,004; NoHighImpact=93). Median overall survival was 3,472 days for HighImpact and 3,669 days for NoHighImpact patients. The log‐rank test yielded χ²=0.18 (p=0.6696), indicating no significant difference in survival between groups.

Conclusion: The analysis was implemented correctly and finds no evidence to support the hypothesis that high‐impact mutations are associated with shorter overall survival.

untried_experiments.hypothesis: Breast cancer receptor subtypes defined by ER, PR, and HER2 status exhibit significant differences in expression of key immune checkpoint genes (PDCD1, CD274, CTLA4).

experiment_plan.objective: Determine whether immune checkpoint gene expression differs across receptor‐defined subtypes.
experiment_plan.steps: 1. Load clinical and gene expression datasets and match by patient barcode. 2. For each patient, define receptor subtype: Luminal A (ER+ & PR+ & HER2−), Luminal B (ER+ & PR+ & HER2+), HER2‐enriched (ER− & PR− & HER2+), Triple‐Negative (ER− & PR− & HER2−). 3. Filter to patients with non‐missing ER, PR, and HER2 IHC status and available expression for PDCD1, CD274, CTLA4. 4. Extract log2 expression values of these three genes for each subtype group. 5. Perform one‐way ANOVA for each gene to test expression differences among subtypes. 6. If ANOVA is significant, run Tukey’s HSD post‐hoc tests to identify pairwise subtype differences. 7. Plot boxplots of gene expression by subtype with significance annotations.
experiment_plan.deliverables: • Table of sample sizes per subtype and gene. • ANOVA tables (F‐statistic, p‐value) for PDCD1, CD274, CTLA4. • Tukey HSD pairwise comparison results. • Boxplots of expression by subtype with annotated p‐values.

untried_experiments.hypothesis: Older age at diagnosis is associated with lower tumor proliferation gene expression, as measured by MKI67 and PCNA.

experiment_plan.objective: Assess the relationship between patient age at diagnosis and expression of proliferation markers.
experiment_plan.steps: 1. Load clinical and gene expression data and merge on patient barcode. 2. Extract age_at_diagnosis and log2 expression for MKI67 and PCNA for each patient. 3. Compute a proliferation score = mean(expression(MKI67), expression(PCNA)). 4. Plot a scatterplot of proliferation score versus age_at_diagnosis with a fitted linear regression line. 5. Compute Pearson and Spearman correlation coefficients between age and proliferation score and record p‐values. 6. Check for linearity and outliers.
experiment_plan.deliverables: • Scatterplot with regression line and confidence band. • Pearson and Spearman correlation coefficients and p‐values. • Table of summary statistics (mean, SD) of proliferation score by age decile.

untried_experiments.hypothesis: Receipt of radiation therapy is associated with a lower incidence of new tumor events after initial treatment.

experiment_plan.objective: Test whether radiation therapy reduces the risk of subsequent tumor events.
experiment_plan.steps: 1. Load clinical data and filter to patients with non‐missing radiation_therapy and new_tumor_event. 2. Create two groups: Radiation = Yes vs No. 3. Tabulate counts of new_tumor_event=Yes/No in each group. 4. Perform Fisher’s exact test on the 2×2 contingency table. 5. Calculate odds ratio and 95% confidence interval. 6. Create a bar chart showing the proportion of patients with new tumor events by radiation status.
experiment_plan.deliverables: • Contingency table of radiation × new tumor event. • Fisher’s exact test result (odds ratio, p‐value). • Bar chart of event proportions by group.

untried_experiments.hypothesis: Patients with high tumor mutation burden (top quartile) exhibit higher CD274 (PD-L1) expression than patients with low mutation burden (bottom quartile).

experiment_plan.objective: Determine if mutation burden correlates positively with PD‐L1 expression.
experiment_plan.steps: 1. Load mutation and gene expression data, match by patient barcode. 2. Count total somatic mutations per patient. 3. Define high‐burden group = top 25% of mutation counts, low‐burden group = bottom 25%. 4. Merge with expression of the CD274 gene for those patients. 5. Compare CD274 expression between groups using a two‐sided Wilcoxon rank‐sum test. 6. Plot a boxplot of CD274 expression for high vs low mutation burden.
experiment_plan.deliverables: • Table of group sizes, median CD274 expression, IQR. • Wilcoxon test statistic and p‐value. • Boxplot of CD274 expression by mutation burden group.

untried_experiments.hypothesis: Patients with TP53 mutations have shorter recurrence‐free survival (time to new tumor event) than patients without TP53 mutations.

experiment_plan.objective: Evaluate the effect of TP53 mutation status on recurrence‐free survival.
experiment_plan.steps: 1. Load clinical and mutations data; identify patients with ≥1 TP53 mutation. 2. Create a binary flag TP53_mut = Yes/No. 3. Fit Kaplan‐Meier curves stratified by TP53_mut status. 6. Perform log‐rank test to compare survival distributions. 7. Plot Kaplan‐Meier curves with confidence intervals.
experiment_plan.deliverables: • Kaplan‐Meier curves for TP53_mutant vs wild‐type. • Log‐rank test statistic and p‐value. • Median recurrence‐free survival times for each group.

untried_experiments.hypothesis: Hormone receptor‐positive patients (ER+ and PR+) have a higher frequency of PIK3CA mutations than hormone receptor‐negative patients.

experiment_plan.objective: Test the association between hormone receptor status and PIK3CA mutation frequency.
experiment_plan.steps: 1. Load clinical and mutation data, merge by patient barcode. 2. experiment_plan.deliverables: • Contingency table of HR status × PIK3CA mutation. • Fisher’s exact test odds ratio and p‐value. • Bar chart of PIK3CA mutation rates in HR+ vs HR− patients.
